s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertional worsening and relief with forward leaning, accompanied by shortness of breath and signs of cardiac involvement
salient_findings: Sharp, stabbing right-sided chest pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward
Shortness of breath on minimal activity
Malar rash and jugular venous distension
Tender anterior chest wall and bibasilar Velcro crackles
Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration
key_facts: 44-year-old woman presented to the emergency department
2 days of sharp, stabbing right-sided chest pain
Chest pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward
Shortness of breath on minimal activity
Chronic right lower-leg swelling
Six months of symmetric wrist stiffness that improved during the day
History of heavy menstrual bleeding and a miscarriage at age 14
Chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses
Placement of a nonretrievable inferior vena cava filter
Obese and mildly tachypneic on examination
Vital signs: temperature 98.6°F, blood pressure 116/91 mm Hg, heart rate 88/min, respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Malar rash and jugular venous distension on examination
Tender anterior chest wall and bibasilar Velcro crackles on examination
Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration on examination
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, platelets 71 × 10^3/mm^3, ESR 55 mm/h, CRP 90.9 mg/L, D-dimer 3.7 µg/mL on laboratory studies

per_call: Acute Coronary Syndrome due to Vasculitis

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and elevated ESR and CRP

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent deep vein thromboses and positive laboratory findings

shortlist.label: Acute Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Sharp, stabbing chest pain relieved by leaning forward and pericardial effusion on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Infective Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Tricuspid valve vegetation on echocardiography and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetric wrist stiffness and elevated ESR and CRP

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 55 mm/h, CRP 90.9 mg/L) are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). Additionally, the patient's history of heavy menstrual bleeding, miscarriage, and chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses suggests a possible underlying autoimmune disorder, which is further supported by the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies (suggested by the history of recurrent thromboses and miscarriage). The patient's cardiac findings, including pericardial effusion and tricuspid regurgitation, can also be seen in SLE.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of recurrent thromboses and miscarriage, which are consistent with Antiphospholipid Syndrome, the presence of a malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers suggest a more systemic autoimmune disorder, such as SLE.

rejected.label: Acute Pericarditis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation of chest pain relieved by leaning forward is consistent with pericarditis, but the presence of other systemic symptoms and findings, such as a malar rash and symmetric wrist stiffness, suggest a more complex autoimmune disorder.

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's blood cultures were negative, and while the transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography showed vegetations on the tricuspid valve, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with an autoimmune disorder than an infectious process.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: The patient's symmetric wrist stiffness that improves during the day is more consistent with SLE or another autoimmune disorder, rather than Rheumatoid Arthritis, which typically worsens with activity.
